title: feat(plugin-audit): a comment thread can be marked resolved and reopened

_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuMsy8fpTCu5kQmHrvVyhAmE)_

repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUJ3ExTXMikbrPFNqD

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none
Flow: dev-thread rule (maintainer 2026-11-20 09:22:50Z 「所有 p1 都按照新规则执行」): the card thread builds itself; L1 and the isolated L2 run in parallel at hand-back.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：后端准备好了「已解决」：一串评论可以标记已解决、再恢复，记下谁解决的、什么时候；往已解决的串里回复会自动恢复。界面在评论栏卡里做，这个改动本身用户看不到。
- 为什么做：评论重做专题第一阶段，评论栏的未解决数字和「显示已解决」「只看我参与的」筛选都靠它。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是一串讨论被误收起，可以再点恢复，任何人回一句也会自动恢复；评论的文字不受影响；能直接撤回这个改动。
- 要你做什么：无（「能看记录的人就能标记」已在 13:25 选定）。

## What changes

`sys_comment` gains the resolution of a thread. A **thread** is one top-level comment (no `parent_id`) together with its replies; its state lives on the top-level row.

| Field | Type | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `is_resolved` | boolean, default `false` | the caller, on a top-level comment only |
| `resolved_by` | lookup `sys_user`, `readonly` | the platform: the session user when `is_resolved` turns `true`, cleared when it turns `false` |
| `resolved_at` | datetime, `readonly` | the platform: the server clock, same rule |

- **Resolve / reopen** = `PATCH` the top-level comment through the data API with `{ "is_resolved": true }` or `false`. Resolving an already-resolved thread changes nothing (the first resolver stays).
- **Who may** (maintainer ruling record 7063285032, option A, reviewed before the decision in the project's fable review): **anyone who may comment on the record may resolve and reopen its threads**. An update that changes nothing but `is_resolved` (beside the row id and the platform stamps `updated_at`, `updated_by`, `resolved_by`, `resolved_at`) is authorized by the rule that admits a new comment — the caller can read the record the thread is on — instead of the author-or-record-editor rule. This is the one, deliberate widening. Any other field beside it still needs the comment's author or an editor of the record. A caller who cannot read the record gets the platform's not-visible refusal (`PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403); a thread naming no record is resolvable by its author only.
- **Only a thread is resolved**: an update naming `is_resolved` on a reply is refused, `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 (field `is_resolved`), its author and a record editor included. A reply's own fields stay editable as before.
- **A new comment is unresolved**: on create the platform sets `is_resolved: false` and clears `resolved_by` / `resolved_at` over a client's values.
- **A reply reopens its thread**: after a reply is inserted (`afterInsert`), when its thread's top-level comment is resolved, the platform updates it back to `is_resolved: false` (system write; the stamp clears the resolver and time). A historical import (`preserveAudit`) does not reopen. A reopen that fails is logged at `error` with the consequence and the fix; the reply stands.
- **Activity**: resolving or reopening writes no entry on the record's activity tab. The comment's own update is recorded as every comment write is (audit ledger plus an activity row whose parent is the comment, per the maintainer ruling on #30213), and the record timeline never draws those.
- **Stored rows**: no migration. The SQL column default is `false` (`applyDeclaredColumnDefault`), so existing rows read unresolved, and `is_resolved: { $ne: true }` also matches a row with no value (pinned below with a NULL row).
- **Where**: the new `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-resolution.ts` holds the stamp, the reply refusal, the resolution-only predicate, the reopen hook and the "involving me" rule; `comment-access-hooks.ts` wires them (the resolution limb of the update gate, the create-side clear, the registrations). `audit-writers.ts` changes by one word: `parseCommentMentions` is exported so the involving-me rule reads `mentions` exactly as the mention notifier does.

### For the comment panel (#36075): field names and query shapes

All through the existing comment read gate, as the caller:

- **The record's threads** — the panel already reads the record's whole discussion in one read (the record page's `discussion` part, "no page size"; or `GET /data/sys_comment` with `thread_id` = `OBJECT:ID`). Group by `parent_id`; the top-level rows carry `is_resolved`, `resolved_by`, `resolved_at`.
- **Unresolved threads only (top-level rows)**: `{ object_name: OBJECT, record_id: ID, parent_id: null, is_resolved: { $ne: true } }` — one statement. Resolved only: same with `is_resolved: true`.
- **Unresolved-thread count** (the icon's number): `count` of that same filter — one `COUNT`. For 3 threads with 1 resolved it answers 2 (pinned).
- ⛔ Not `{ parent_id: { is_resolved: … } }` to fetch replies of open threads: `sys_comment` carries an object-scoped read middleware, so the engine reads ids under a cap instead of a subquery. Filter the loaded replies by their thread instead.
- **"Involving me"** — no server query in phase 1 (the review's implementation choice: the panel holds the whole thread set, and the query engine serves no condition that selects a parent row by its children). The rule, exported as `threadsInvolvingUser(rows, userId)` and pinned in `comment-resolution.test.ts`: a thread (identified by its top-level comment's id) involves the user when
  1. the top-level comment's `author_id` is the user (started it), or
  2. any reply in the thread has `author_id` the user (replied), or
  3. the user's id is in the `mentions` of the top-level comment or of any reply (a JSON array of ids, or of `{ id }` objects; unparseable reads as none) — **including a user who never wrote in the thread**.
  A reply belongs to the thread reached by following `parent_id` through the loaded rows; a reply whose chain leaves the loaded set is in no thread. The rule ignores resolution; compose it with the resolved filter.
- Phase 2's cross-record "involving me" query (the view-wide feed) needs its own decision: an engine condition selecting parents by children, or a platform-kept participant list.

## Tests

- `comment-resolution.integration.test.ts` (new; real kernel, ObjectQL, AuditPlugin, SQLite): stamp and clear with the server clock; a client's resolver/time replaced by the stamp, or stripped and reported in `droppedFields` without one; first resolver kept; new comment unresolved; reply refusal on the wire (`mapDataError` → 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, nothing written); a reply reopens a resolved thread; a reply into an open thread and a new top-level comment change nothing; filter + count (3 threads, 1 resolved → 2); a NULL row reads unresolved; no new row on the record's activity stream.
- `comment-access-hooks.test.ts` (new top-level `describe`, sharing double that denies edit): a reader resolves and reopens another user's thread without the parent-edit question; the stamps beside it keep it resolution-only; the same reader with `body` or `mentions` beside `is_resolved` (and a bare body edit) is refused 403 `RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`; a non-reader gets 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`; a dangling thread is its author's only; a multi-row resolution needs every row; reply refusal for author, editor and reader; create clears a client's resolution.
- `comment-resolution.test.ts` (new): the involving-me rule (started, replied, nested reply, mentioned on root, mentioned in a reply only, others' threads, orphan reply, unknown user); `isResolutionOnlyUpdate`; the stamp's import, system and non-boolean arms; the reopen failure logged at `error`; an import does not reopen.

## Acceptance notes

- A custom permission set that grants `create` but not `edit` on `sys_comment` can post but not resolve: resolving is an update at the object level. `member_default` grants edit.
- Portal or guest users who can read a record and comment can also resolve its threads under option A (named in the review; not measured whether such deployments exist).
- Re-pointing a reply's `parent_id` into a resolved thread does not reopen it; only an inserted reply does.
- Resolving is recorded on the comment's own audit trail, by the resolver; the reopen a reply triggers is a system write.

## Verification

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/comment-resolution.integration.test.ts` — 10 passed, including "a reply posted into a resolved thread reopens it" and the 3-threads-1-resolved count of 2.
